I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption experiments were conducted using a BSD-VVS&DVS gravimetric vapor adsorption analyzer. Samples were degassed at 200°C for 3 hours, followed by measuring the hydrogen adsorption isotherms at 77K over a pressure range of 0-50 bar.
I1.location: main, p. 2, Section 2.3 Hydrogen Adsorption Measurement (results in Table 2 and Fig. 4a, p. 4)

I2.quote: In this study, we prepared a series of hollow porous carbon spheres using biogas slurry as a raw material, varying factors such as activation temperature and KOH-to-CS mass ratio during the activation phase.
I2.location: main, p. 5, Section 4 Conclusions (the H2-measured samples CS800-4 and CS850-4.5 are KOH-activated members of this carbon series; Table 2, p. 4)

I3.quote: The resulting materials, CS850-4.5 and CS800-4, achieved high gravimetric H2 uptake of 4.5 wt% (77 K, 50 bar) and volumetric H2 uptake of 25.9 g/L (77 K, 30 bar), respectively.
I3.location: main, p. 1, Abstract (also Table 2 and Fig. 4a/4b axes, p. 4)

I4.quote: CS850-4.5, with an activation temperature of 850°C and an activation ratio of 4.5, features a high BET surface area (2140 m²/g), micropore area (1522 m²/g)
I4.location: main, p. 5, Section 4 Conclusions; Table 1, p. 2 (column SBET (m2/g): CS800-4 = 1314, CS850-4.5 = 2142)

I5.quote: Achieving a balance between cost-effectiveness and high performance in hydrogen storage materials is a significant challenge.

notes: Conference proceedings paper (ICAE2024, Energy Proceedings) with original data, not a review. record.json is_retracted is false and the text carries no retraction notice. The paper makes no statement that its H2 uptake values were published before. The instrument is called a gravimetric analyzer by the authors; either gravimetric or volumetric meets I1. Samples CS800-4 and CS850-4.5 have both a BET area (Table 1) and H2 isotherms at 77 K up to 30 bar shown (Fig. 4), with 50 bar stated for CS850-4.5. Minor internal inconsistencies that do not affect eligibility: CS850-4.5 BET is 2142 in Table 1 but 2140 in the Conclusions; its 1 bar uptake is 1.9 wt% in Table 2 but 2.3 wt% in Section 3.4; Vmicro is given in m3/g where cm3/g is meant.
